To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have determined the structure of TTR complexed with AcCoA.
the TTR protein complexed with AcCoA is a dimer and that the TTR dimer is the active form of this protein.
the TTR fusion proteins complexed with AcCoA were crystallized and that the structures of the native and SeMet TTR derivatives were solved by MAD and SAD phasing methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the purification, crystallization and structure determination of TTR and TTR-AcCoA complex.
the structure determination of the native TTR-AcCoA complex, the SeMet TTR-Ac-CoA complex and the native SeMet TTR complex.
the crystallization of native and SeMet TTR derivatives in complex with AcCoa and the collection of diffraction data from these crystals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the crystal structure of the TTR-AcCoA complex will be solved in the near future.
the P2( 1) and C2 crystal forms of the TTR fusion AcCoA complex are isomorphous and belong to the same crystal system.
the crystal structure of TTR complexed with AcCoA will provide the molecular basis for understanding the mechanism of action of TTR and its role in the detoxification of tabtoxin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TTR has been overproduced and crystallized in both native and SeMet forms and that diffraction-quality crystals have been grown.

we were able to successfully crystallize native and SeMet TTR fusion proteins complexed with AcCoA and to collect diffraction data from these crystals to 1. 55 A resolution, which will facilitate our future structural studies of TTR.
we have obtained crystals of native and SeMet TTR fusion proteins complexed with AcCoA and have determined the unit-cell parameters and space group.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to obtain crystals of TTR complexed with its natural ligand, AcCoA, in a reductive crystallization environment.
the SeMet TTR fusion protein crystallizes in two different forms.
it is possible to produce SeMet derivatives in the presence of a cofactor and the SeMet derivative crystallized under reductive conditions.
